Bayern had taken the lead through the teenage Germany winger Lennart Karl, but Elversberg – who won their opening two matches in their maiden top-flight campaign – levelled things up just after the hour mark thanks to a stunning curling effort from Maurice Krattenmacher.

Kane scored 36 league goals last season, but after drawing a blank in his first two matches he told Dazn: “That’s football – sometimes you have to wait more than you’d have expected. It was nice to get the goal and the three points. It’s a tough place so we’re happy with the win. We probably haven’t reached our top level yet, but it’s still early days.”

RB Leipzig bounced back from their midweek Champions League defeat at Como by thumping Hamburg 5-0 at home. The Norway winger Antonio Nusa was the best of the bunch for the hosts, scoring one goal and setting up two more, including one for Christopher Nkunku, his first since returning to Leipzig in August.

Tidiam Gomis, Willi Orban and Rômulo also got on the scoresheet for Leipzig, who climbed to fifth in the table. Hamburg’s third heavy defeat in a row leaves the six-times German champions bottom of the table with a -12 goal difference.

In Italy, Juventus suffered a 3-2 defeat after a frantic finish at Sassuolo on Sunday. Sassuolo broke the deadlock in the 65th minute when Nemanja Matic slipped a precise ⁠pass into the area for Sebastiano Esposito, who finished coolly.

Juventus levelled in the 82nd ​minute after goalkeeper Arijanet Muric misjudged a cross, ‌allowing Edon Zhegrova to tap ‌into an empty net. The hosts retook the lead through their Scottish striker Kieron Bowie, who curled a first-time effort into the corner in the 89th minute.

Zhegrova appeared to have rescued a point for Juventus when he fired home from the edge of the area in stoppage time, but Sassuolo had the final say. Four minutes into injury time, Vasilije Adzic curled a superb finish into the far corner to seal victory for Alberto Aquilani’s side with virtually the ‌last kick of the game.
